quarterly_data.signal: ST's 20-F: its largest customer, Apple, accounted for 17.7%, 14.5% and 12.3% of net revenues in 2025, 2024 and 2023, reported within the AM&S, P&D, EMP and RFOC segments; no individual customer represented more than 10% of trade accounts receivable at December 31, 2025 or 2024. ST sells to over 200,000 customers; its major customers include (in alphabetical order) Apple, Bosch, Continental, Denso, HP, Mobileye, Samsung, SpaceX, Tesla and Vitesco.
quarterly_data.figure: Apple 17.7% of 2025 net revenues (14.5% in 2024, 12.3% in 2023)

quarterly_data.signal: ST's 20-F, full-year 2025 by segment: Power and Discrete (P&D) revenue was $1,685 million, down 31.5% from $2,461 million, with an operating loss of $275 million (operating income of $263 million in 2024); RF Optical Communications (RFOC) revenue was $1,436 million, down 4.9% from $1,511 million, with operating income of $265 million. Unused capacity charges were $416 million in 2025 versus $370 million in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 P&D revenue $1,685 million (-31.5%), operating loss $275 million; RFOC revenue $1,436 million (-4.9%), operating income $265 million

quarterly_data.signal: ST's 20-F on sourcing and capacity: in 2025 ST subcontracted approximately 25% of the value of its total silicon production to external foundries and plans to keep sourcing silicon from external foundries and OSATs. Purchase commitments for outsourced foundry wafers totalled $774 million at December 31, 2025, of which $555 million falls due in 2026. ST had approximately $1.3 billion of outstanding orders for equipment and other assets for delivery in 2026; capital expenditure payments, net of proceeds from sales, capital grants and other contributions, were $1,844 million in 2025 versus $2,642 million in 2024. ST entered 2026 with a backlog higher than it had entering 2025 (it entered 2025 with a lower backlog than entering 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 25% of silicon production value outsourced; foundry wafer commitments $774 million ($555 million in 2026); equipment orders approximately $1.3 billion; 2025 net capex payments $1,844 million

quarterly_data.signal: ST's 20-F on new fabs: the new high-volume 200mm SiC manufacturing facility for power devices and modules in Catania, Italy is a planned investment of EUR 5 billion in capital expenditure, and on October 13, 2025 the European Commission granted ST Integrated Production Facility status under the European Chips Act. The joint 300mm front-end facility with GlobalFoundries in Crolles, France has an overall projected cost of EUR 7.5 billion for capital expenditure, maintenance and ancillary costs. The full buildout of the Sanan ST JV (200mm SiC device manufacturing in China, created with Sanan Optoelectronics on June 7, 2023 and consolidated by ST) is expected to cost about $3.2 billion, including capital expenditures of about $2.4 billion over a 5 year period as of 2023; $433 million of the JV's property, plant and equipment was on ST's balance sheet at December 31, 2025 ($316 million a year earlier).
quarterly_data.figure: Catania SiC plant EUR 5 billion capex; Crolles 300mm fab with GlobalFoundries EUR 7.5 billion projected cost; Sanan ST JV buildout about $3.2 billion (about $2.4 billion capex); JV PP&E $433 million

quarterly_data.signal: Partner Innoscience: ST's 20-F lists among recent developments that 'On March 31, we announced the signature of an agreement on GaN technology development and manufacturing with Innoscience', which ST describes as the world leader in 8-inch GaN-on-Si high-performance low-cost manufacturing (the filing does not print the year of the announcement).

connects_to.relationship: multi-year semiconductor supply engagement for AWS cloud/AI data-center compute infrastructure (power, optical interconnect, MCU, sensing)

contracts.signal: ST's 20-F: on February 9, 2026 ST announced an expanded strategic collaboration with Amazon Web Services through a multi-year, multi-billion USD commercial engagement serving several product categories, to enable new high-performance compute infrastructure for cloud and AI data centers. On February 6, 2026 ST issued warrants to AWS for up to 24.8 million ordinary shares, vesting in tranches over the term of the agreement, with vesting substantially tied to payments for ST products and services purchased by AWS and its affiliates; AWS may exercise them over a seven-year period.
contracts.units: warrants for up to 24.8 million ordinary shares, vesting with AWS purchases
contracts.type: commercial engagement with purchase-linked customer warrants

players.product: Vertically integrated SiC substrates, epitaxy and power chips (Hunan Sanan 6-inch and 8-inch SiC lines, GaN-on-Si); 8-inch SiC substrates from Chongqing Sanan for the Anyifa 8-inch SiC epitaxy and chip joint venture

connects_to.relationship: 200mm SiC substrates for the Sanan ST JV, the dedicated 200mm SiC device foundry that produces exclusively for STMicroelectronics

contracts.signal: ST's 20-F: ST and Sanan Optoelectronics jointly created the Sanan ST JV in 2023 for high-volume 200mm SiC device manufacturing in China; the JV will produce SiC devices exclusively for ST using ST's proprietary SiC manufacturing process technology, serving as a dedicated foundry to support ST's demand for Chinese customers, and Sanan Optoelectronics will build a separate 200mm SiC substrate manufacturing facility to fulfill the JV's needs. ST is the JV's primary beneficiary and fully consolidates it.
contracts.units: 200mm SiC substrates from a separate substrate manufacturing facility Sanan Optoelectronics will build
